title: Distribution, Research, and Pricing - Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA - Marketing-Information Management
subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Why do businesses primarily need marketing data?
options: To satisfy government tax reporting requirements
To monitor employee work hours
To reduce the risk of making incorrect business decisions by providing insights into consumer behavior
To ensure they pay the correct tariffs on imported goods
questions.explain: Marketing information management involves gathering and analyzing data to make informed, data-driven decisions that minimize business risks and meet consumer needs.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Information that is collected for the very first time to solve a specific marketing problem is called:
options: Secondary data
Primary data
Historical data
Demographic data
questions.explain: Primary data is original research data gathered specifically to address the research problem at hand.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A company uses a previously published industry report from a research firm to understand market trends. What type of data is this?
options: Primary data
Qualitative data
Secondary data
Experimental data
questions.explain: Secondary data is information that was already collected by someone else for another purpose but can be used for the current research.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which of the following is a key advantage of using secondary data over primary data?
options: It is always perfectly relevant to the specific problem at hand.
It is usually cheaper and faster to obtain.
It provides a competitive advantage because rivals cannot access it.
It ensures complete privacy of the company's customers.
questions.explain: Secondary data is existing data, meaning it does not require the time and financial resources necessary to design and conduct a brand new primary study.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which research method involves bringing together a small group of 6 to 12 people to discuss a specific product or marketing strategy under the guidance of a moderator?
options: Observation
Surveying
A Focus Group
An Experiment
questions.explain: A focus group is a qualitative research technique that involves an interactive group discussion led by a trained moderator.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Quantitative research focuses heavily on:
options: In-depth emotional responses and personal feelings
Numerical data, statistics, and large sample sizes to find patterns
Observing how people use a product in their homes
Focus groups and informal interviews
questions.explain: Quantitative research uses mathematical analyses, statistics, and numerical data to quantify opinions, behaviors, and other defined variables.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A marketer tracks how many times users click on a specific website ad to determine which version is most effective. What kind of data is being monitored here?
options: Psychographic data
Behavioral analytics data
Qualitative secondary data
Focus group data
questions.explain: Click-through rates are a form of behavioral analytics data, tracking actual user actions to make data-driven marketing decisions.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: To gauge internal sales performance, what data source should a marketing manager rely on first?
options: Competitors' published financial reports
Census demographic reports
The company's own Customer Relationship Management (CRM) records and sales reports
Focus groups about potential future products
questions.explain: Internal records like CRM systems and sales reports offer the most direct, accurate data regarding a company's own sales performance and customer interactions.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which of the following describes 'Big Data' in the context of marketing information management?
options: Data sets that are small but deeply insightful
Extremely large and complex data sets that require advanced software to process and analyze for patterns
Data collected only from print magazines and newspapers
Only information that pertains to macroeconomics
questions.explain: Big Data refers to massive volumes of structured and unstructured data that can be analyzed computationally to reveal patterns, trends, and associations relating to human behavior.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: If a research study repeatedly produces the exact same results when conducted under identical conditions, the study is considered to be highly:
options: Valid
Reliable
Subjective
Biased
questions.explain: Reliability refers to the consistency of a measure. A reliable research method will yield the same results if repeated under identical conditions.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: When a marketing survey actually measures what it claims or is intended to measure, the survey is said to possess:
options: Validity
Reliability
Sample bias
Secondary scope
questions.explain: Validity indicates accuracy—whether a study or instrument correctly measures the specific concept it was designed to measure.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of psychographic data?
options: A customer's age and income bracket
The geographic region where the customer lives
A customer's hobbies, values, and lifestyle choices
The frequency of a customer's product purchases over a year
questions.explain: Psychographics deal with psychological attributes such as lifestyle, personality, values, opinions, and interests.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A mystery shopper evaluating customer service in a retail store is participating in what type of primary research method?
options: Observation
Experimentation
Focus Group
Secondary Data Analysis
questions.explain: Mystery shopping is a form of observation research where researchers monitor or record behaviors in a natural setting to gather information.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: What is the primary function of a Marketing Information System (MkIS)?
options: To replace the marketing manager with Artificial Intelligence
To continuously gather, sort, analyze, evaluate, and distribute pertinent, timely information to marketing decision-makers
To track employee payroll and benefits within the marketing department
To automatically write and distribute press releases to the media
questions.explain: An MkIS is a structured system combining people, equipment, and procedures specifically designed to manage marketing data continuously for decision-making.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: When conducting market research, 'sampling' refers to:
options: Distributing free bite-sized portions of food to supermarket shoppers
Selecting a representative group from a larger population to participate in a study
Collecting data only during the summer months
Borrowing data entirely from secondary sources
questions.explain: In research, sampling is the process of selecting a predetermined number of elements from a population to draw conclusions about the whole population.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: What data should a marketing team monitor to see what percentage of total industry sales their brand currently holds?
options: Return on Investment (ROI)
Customer Retention Rate
Market Share
Inventory Turnover
questions.explain: Market share is a company's total sales expressed as a percentage of the total sales for the entire industry or specific market.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which of the following surveys provides qualitative data rather than quantitative?
options: A poll asking 'On a scale of 1-10, how satisfied are you?'
An open-ended questionnaire asking 'Describe why you love this product.'
A multiple choice test asking respondents their income range
A tracking script noting how many seconds users spend on a webpage
questions.explain: Open-ended questions gather descriptive, non-numerical responses that provide deep insights into feelings and opinions, which characterizes qualitative data.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: How is environmental scanning used in marketing decision-making?
options: It involves analyzing external forces (like economic, social, or technological changes) to identify opportunities and threats.
It is the process of physically reviewing store shelves for cleanliness.
It is used exclusively to evaluate internal corporate strengths.
It scans customer receipts to issue refunds.
questions.explain: Environmental scanning is the ongoing tracking of trends and occurrences in an organization's internal and external environment that bear on its success.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: What does demographic data focus on when monitored for marketing effectiveness?
options: Consumer attitudes, values, and lifestyle preferences
Statistical characteristics of populations such as age, gender, education, and income
Online purchase histories and clicking behaviors
The specific geographic coordinates of consumer homes
questions.explain: Demographics strictly refer to statistical data relating to the population and particular groups within it, like age, income, and education.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A company performs an A/B test by sending two slightly different emails to their contact list and measuring which gets more clicks. This is an example of:
options: Secondary research
Experimental research
Observational research
Demographic research
questions.explain: Experimental research (like A/B testing) involves manipulating one variable (the email design) to test a hypothesis and measure the direct effect on another variable (the click rate).
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA
